name: 3 5 7 Poker
description: Three-stage Guts variant: stage one 3 cards (threes wild), stage two 5 cards (fives wild), stage three 7 cards (sevens wild). At each stage players declare in or out; only player in scores a leg; multiple in then best hand wins and losers match the pot. First to three legs wins the pot.
duration: Variable (until one player reaches three legs)

history.origins: Guts-style poker variant from the United States where 3-5-7 cards are dealt with corresponding wild cards in each round.
timeline: Described in modern poker variant references as a three-stage guts-style game with 3, 5, and 7-card hands and stage-specific wild cards.

setup.deck: Standard 52-card pack without jokers; the same deck as base Guts is used for all three stages (3, 5, and 7 cards).

rules.objective: Be the first to collect three legs: either be the only player to stay in at a stage (score one leg) or win a showdown when multiple stay in (losers match the pot); first to three legs wins the entire pot.
rules.gameplay: Three stages. Stage one: all ante, three cards dealt face down to each player; players declare in or out (sequence or simultaneous). If one stays in they score a leg; if two or more stay in they compare hands (triplets beat pairs beat nothing; threes wild), loser(s) pay pot to winner(s). Stage two: two more cards dealt (five total); fives wild; best five-card poker hand wins among those in; same payment rule. Stage three: two more cards (seven total); sevens wild; best five-card from seven wins; same rule. If no one has three legs, everyone antes again and redeal from three cards. First to three legs takes the pot.
keyRules: All ante to start; three stages with 3, then 5, then 7 cards per player.
At each stage players declare in or out; only player in scores a leg; multiple in then showdown, loser(s) match pot to winner(s).
Stage 1: threes wild, no straights/flushes; triplets beat pairs beat high cards. Stages 2–3: fives then sevens wild, standard five-card poker ranking.
First to three legs wins the pot; if no one has three, redeal and re-ante.
